lines.text: Welcome, Gen-AI Creators! Today you will find out what is really happening inside a chatbot.
Generative AI is a computer program that creates new text, pictures or sounds.
It learned patterns from a huge number of examples.
Chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini are generative AI.
A chatbot writes its answer one small piece at a time.
Each time, it guesses which word is most likely to come next.
It is like a super-powered version of the autocomplete on a phone keyboard.
AI is great for ideas, explanations and first drafts.
It can also be confidently wrong, and it does not really know you or today’s news.
You are the boss, so you always check its work.
Never type real names, phone numbers, addresses, passwords or Aadhaar numbers into an AI tool.
Never paste private documents or photos of your friends.
If you would not pin it on the school notice board, keep it out of AI.
If you are under 13, watch the teacher’s screen and use the Kitabash AI helper in the lesson.
If you are 13 to 17, you may use ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot or Perplexity with a parent’s permission.
Here we ask the helper to finish a sentence about the monsoon in Mumbai.
It picks the words that most often come next in the text it learned from.
Notice the honest part: it cannot see Mumbai today, it is only predicting.
This time the AI sounds very sure of itself, but the answer is a famous myth.
Astronauts say the Great Wall is far too thin to see from the Moon.
Sounding confident is not the same as being correct, so we always check.
Start with three simple kinds of prompt: ask for ideas, ask for an explanation, and ask it to create.
Read every answer and ask yourself one question: is this actually true and useful?
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
